newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe welcomes end to French truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Juppe welcomes end to French truckers' strike.

text.p: Prime Minister Alain Juppe welcomed the apparent end to a truck drivers' strike that has paralysed France's roads for 12 days and called for a rapid return to normal.
"I am happy that the efforts made by all negotiating partners are now apparently crowned by success," Juppe told reporters at his town hall in Bordeaux. "I think a balanced solution has been found."

"The situation must return to normal as fast as possible now because many companies are suffering," Juppe said. "The economy is suffering and given the current level of unemployment, all this must become just a memory soon."

In Paris, the national road traffic information centre reported that only 46 out of 250 roadblocks remained across France at 1730 GMT on Friday as drivers voted with their wheels and headed home before the weekend.

Juppe said the drivers, who won the right to retire at 55, full pay for loading, standby and compulsory rest time and several other concessions, had "many legitimate demands". But he said many road haulage firms were in a fragile position.
"I think a balanced outcome has been found," he added.
